candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Epistola ad Adelphium
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Adelphium (Letter to Adelphius, Bishop and Confessor: Against the Arians), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Adelphium (c. 350 AD)

'For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin' — Athanasius marks pepeirasmenon kata panta kath' homoiotēta chōris hamartias (tempted in all-things according-to-likeness without sin) as the Hebrews-formal-statement of Christ's-sinlessness-with-genuine-human-experience. The kata panta (in all-things) excludes Apollinarian-reduction (no human-aspect-missing); the kath' homoiotēta (according to likeness) excludes Docetic-non-genuineness; the chōris hamartias (without sin) excludes Adoptionist-or-Pelagian denial of Christ's-moral-perfection. Tewahedo Holy-Friday meditation cites Heb 4:15 + Rom 8:3 (homoiōmati-sarkos) as the sinless-but-tempted Pauline-Hebrews-pair.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Adelphium. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

'For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin' — Athanasius marks pepeirasmenon kata panta kath' homoiotēta chōris hamartias (tempted in all-things according-to-likeness without sin) as the Hebrews-formal-statement of Christ's-sinlessness-with-genuine-human-experience. The kata panta (in all-things) excludes Apollinarian-reduction (no human-aspect-missing); the kath' homoiotēta (according to likeness) excludes Docetic-non-genuineness; the chōris hamartias (without sin) excludes Adoptionist-or-Pelagian denial of Christ's-moral-perfection. Tewahedo Holy-Friday meditation cites Heb 4:15 + Rom 8:3 (homoiōmati-sarkos) as the sinless-but-tempted Pauline-Hebrews-pair.
